name: The Tempest
kicker: Shakespeare’s late play · A sorcerer’s island of shipwreck and magic
briefing: A deposed Duke of Milan uses magic to shipwreck his enemies on the enchanted island where he has lived in exile for twelve years. With help from the spirit Ariel and the grudging service of the monster Caliban, Prospero plots not revenge but reconciliation, arranging a marriage for his daughter, Miranda, before giving up his magic for good.

qb.tip: A fourth Regular High School hit that matched this query was actually a tossup on “shipwrecks” that only name-drops this play in its giveaway — it’s excluded from the sample below. Caliban and the comic drunkards Stephano and Trinculo show up more often in the real clues than Prospero’s magic does.

sample.note: 5 real QBReader tossups (2 Middle School/Easy High School + 3 Regular High School, power-marked); a 4th Regular HS hit on a different answer line, “shipwrecks,” is excluded

tossups.p: This play’s title event strands a group of Neapolitan nobles returning from a royal wedding in Tunis on an enchanted island. Its sorcerer protagonist was set adrift on that same island twelve years earlier after his brother stole his title as Duke of Milan.
tossups.r: That protagonist’s spirit servant, Ariel, carries out his magic, while a monstrous servant named Caliban resents his control. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the magician Prospero.

tossups.p: This play’s airy spirit was once imprisoned inside a cloven pine tree by a witch named Sycorax [“SIK-uh-raks”] before being freed by the island’s new ruler. That same spirit later disguises itself as a harpy to torment a group of shipwrecked lords with an illusory feast.
tossups.r: Ariel ultimately helps Prospero reclaim his dukedom and reunite with the outside world. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play set on a magical island.

tossups.p: This play’s drunken butler, Stephano, is mistaken for a god who fell from the moon by the island’s monstrous native. That native joins Stephano and the jester Trinculo in a failed plot to murder the island’s ruler.
tossups.r: Caliban is the son of a dead witch named Sycorax. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which a magician named Prospero controls the spirit Ariel.

tossups.p: During a lavish masque celebrating a betrothal in this play, spirits appear as the goddesses Iris, Ceres, and Juno before the magician abruptly ends the celebration. That magician then declares that “our revels now are ended” and that people are “such stuff as dreams are made on.”
tossups.r: The betrothal is between his daughter Miranda and a shipwrecked prince, Ferdinand. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play.

tossups.p: Antonio and Sebastian plot to murder a sleeping king in this play, but Ariel wakes the old counselor Gonzalo in time to stop them. Years earlier, that same Gonzalo had secretly supplied this play’s protagonist with books as he was set adrift at sea.
tossups.r: The protagonist relies on those books for the sorcery that lets him conjure the storm that opens this play. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play starring the magician Prospero.

tossups.p: This play’s heroine has lived on an isolated island since early childhood and has barely seen any humans besides her father and a monstrous servant. Upon meeting a shipwrecked prince for the first time, she wonders aloud whether he might be “a spirit.”
tossups.r: That heroine, Miranda, soon falls in love with Ferdinand. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which Miranda’s father, Prospero, approves their marriage.

tossups.p: A spirit in this play sings “Full Fathom Five” to a prince who believes his father has drowned, though the king is secretly alive elsewhere on the island. This play’s title event is magically conjured to strand a group of Neapolitan and Milanese nobles.
tossups.r: That spirit, Ariel, serves the island’s exiled sorcerer. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the magician Prospero and the monster Caliban.

tossups.p: This play’s protagonist was deposed as Duke of Milan by his own brother, Antonio, and set adrift at sea with his infant daughter. Twelve years later, that protagonist uses sorcery to shipwreck his usurping brother on the same island where he found refuge.
tossups.r: He is aided by a spirit named Ariel and served, less willingly, by a monster named Caliban. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play about a magician’s revenge and forgiveness.

tossups.p: This play’s monstrous character is the son of a dead witch and resents being enslaved by the island’s ruler after once being taught language by that ruler’s daughter. He later tries, and fails, to lead a drunken rebellion against his master.
tossups.r: That character, Caliban, shares the island with a spirit named Ariel. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which the magician Prospero controls them both.

tossups.p: The poet W. H. Auden wrote a long response to this play called _The Sea and the Mirror_. In a famous postcolonial adaptation of this play by the writer Aimé Césaire [“eh-MAY say-ZEHR”], its monstrous character demands to be called “X.”
tossups.r: That monstrous character, Caliban, serves the magician Prospero alongside the spirit Ariel. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play.

tossups.p: In a 2010 film version of this play, Helen Mirren played a gender-swapped version of the sorcerer, while Djimon Hounsou played the monstrous Caliban. This play’s plot may draw on real accounts of a 1609 shipwreck in Bermuda.
tossups.r: Its sorcerer, Prospero, conjures the storm that gives this play its name. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the spirit Ariel.

tossups.p: Many scholars consider this to be the last play Shakespeare wrote entirely on his own, and its Epilogue has often been read as his farewell to the stage. In that Epilogue, the protagonist begs the audience to “set me free” with their applause.
tossups.r: That protagonist, the magician Prospero, ultimately chooses forgiveness over revenge. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play.

tossups.p: This play is unusual among Shakespeare’s works for taking place in a single location over the course of just a few hours. Its plot is set in motion when a magician conjures a storm to strand his usurping brother on his island of exile.
tossups.r: That magician, Prospero, is aided by the spirit Ariel and served by the monster Caliban. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play about a sorcerer’s island.

tossups.p: This play’s magician secretly arranges for his daughter to fall in love with the son of the king who helped usurp his dukedom years earlier. That magician ultimately forgives his enemies, vows to break his staff, and frees his spirit servant.
tossups.r: Prospero’s daughter Miranda is engaged to Ferdinand, the son of King Alonso, by the end of the play. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the monster Caliban.

tossups.p: This play opens with sailors struggling against a magically conjured storm that wrecks a ship carrying the King of Naples and his court. Its magician protagonist, exiled to a remote island twelve years earlier, uses that storm to bring his enemies within his power at last.
tossups.r: He is served by the spirit Ariel and the monster Caliban. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which Prospero gives up sorcery after reuniting his daughter Miranda with the outside world.

clues.t: Its magician protagonist, Prospero, is the exiled Duke of Milan
Caliban, a monstrous servant enslaved on the island, resents Prospero’s control
Ariel, a spirit of the air, carries out Prospero’s magic in exchange for eventual freedom
A magical storm, conjured by Prospero, shipwrecks his enemies on his island
Ends with Prospero’s daughter, Miranda, engaged to the shipwrecked prince Ferdinand
Antonio, Prospero’s brother, stole his dukedom and is among the shipwrecked nobles
Alonso, the King of Naples, searches the island for his son Ferdinand, believing him drowned
The drunken butler Stephano and jester Trinculo team up with Caliban against Prospero
Sycorax, Caliban’s dead mother, once ruled the island and imprisoned Ariel in a tree
After ending a wedding masque, Prospero declares that “we are such stuff as dreams are made on”
Prospero ultimately forgives his enemies, vows to break his magic staff, and frees Ariel
Gonzalo, an honest old counselor, is woken by Ariel in time to foil a murder plot against the sleeping King Alonso
Prospero was set adrift with infant Miranda and spent twelve years in exile before the play begins
Ariel sings “Full Fathom Five” to Ferdinand, who wrongly believes his father has drowned
In the Epilogue, Prospero asks the audience to “set me free” with their applause
Aldous Huxley’s _Brave New World_ takes its title from a line spoken by Miranda in this play
W. H. Auden’s long poem _The Sea and the Mirror_ responds to this play
A postcolonial adaptation by the writer Aimé Césaire reimagines Caliban demanding to be called “X”
Djimon Hounsou played Caliban in a 2010 film adaptation opposite Helen Mirren
Some scholars connect this play’s Act 4 wedding masque to a real royal wedding of its era
Unusually for Shakespeare, this play’s action unfolds in one place over just a few hours, following the classical unities

trap.title: Which monster, which spirit?
trap.body: Caliban and Ariel are easy to swap. Caliban is the earthy, resentful “monster” born on the island who wants Prospero gone; Ariel is the airy spirit who carries out Prospero’s magic in exchange for eventual freedom. Clues about drunken plotting or being enslaved point to Caliban; clues about songs, illusions, or flying point to Ariel.
trap.fix: Ask whether the clue describes a grudge and a wish to rebel (Caliban) or a magical task performed for Prospero (Ariel). Either way, the answer to this whole tossup is the play, not either character.
